_metadata.independence: I read only u11-blind-input.json; no other file, repository search, web lookup or API was used.

hints.reason: The king is a face card, and the lion is the king of the jungle / The Lion King.

best_available.why: Both routes are immediate and universally known.

pairs.pair_note: Single strong hint; nothing to fix.

hints.reason: Tarot is a card deck, and The Moon is one of its best-known major-arcana cards (tarot also carries a general lunar/mystical mood).

best_available.why: Card side is certain; the Moon card is familiar enough to most players through general tarot imagery.

pairs.pair_note: Moon side relies on knowing The Moon tarot card, but the mystical association carries non-experts too.

hints.reason: Mickey Mouse makes the mouse side immediate, but the card side only reaches via Disney gift cards or the niche Lorcana trading-card game.

best_available.why: Only hint offered; mouse side is excellent but card is a weak afterthought.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The card route to Disney is not a familiar phrase; a player would need CARD to be the only leftover word.

hints.reason: Card game is a compound and game night is a familiar phrase.
Poker is a card game and poker night is a stock phrase.

best_available.why: More specific than GAME; poker night evokes the cards-on-the-table scene directly.

pairs.pair_note: Two good hints; GAME is a little broader but still fair.

hints.reason: Ocean's Eleven is a well-known casino film, but the card side only reaches through the casino setting or an ace counting eleven in blackjack.

best_available.why: Only hint offered; the casino-heist setting gives card a thin but real foothold.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Clever title route, but the card side needs an explanation most players will not produce.

hints.reason: A deck of cards, and pirates on the deck of their ship.

best_available.why: Clean double meaning that reaches both words directly.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent single hint.

hints.reason: Diamonds are a card suit and a diamond ring is the classic ring.
Wedding ring is a compound and wedding cards are a standard greeting-card category.

best_available.why: Suit plus diamond ring is the tighter double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Both hints solid.

hints.reason: Chip card / chip-and-PIN and SIM cards carry chips; robots run on computer chips.

best_available.why: Both sides are everyday compounds.

pairs.pair_note: Good single hint.

hints.reason: Rock-paper-scissors reaches rock, and card is stiff paper (greeting cards, cardstock).

best_available.why: Famous game phrase plus a material near-synonym.

pairs.pair_note: Good hint; material route is a legitimate shared property here.

hints.reason: Valentine card is a compound and roses are the Valentine's Day flower.

best_available.why: One shared scene reaches both words instantly.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: Card table and table salt are both stock compounds.

best_available.why: Two familiar compounds.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Card trick is immediate, but shadow only reaches via hand-shadow puppetry or 'a trick of the light'.

best_available.why: Only hint offered; shadow puppets as a trick is thin but imaginable.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Shadow side lacks a phrase or scene a player would name.

hints.reason: Poker is a card game, and a card shark / poker shark is the familiar term for a hustling player.

best_available.why: The card-shark idiom makes both targets natural.

pairs.pair_note: Good; the pair itself is the idiom.

hints.reason: Card dealer is immediate, but nothing recognizable links dealer to snake (snake-oil goes with 'salesman', not 'dealer').

best_available.why: Only hint offered; it does not reach snake.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Needs a new hint; the one offered is wholly one-sided.

hints.reason: Solitaire is the one-player card game, and Spider Solitaire is the widely known Windows variant.

best_available.why: Spider Solitaire is a household name for PC users.

pairs.pair_note: Good; spider side is slightly weaker for non-computer players.

hints.reason: Easter cards are a standard greeting-card category and Easter is the spring holiday.

best_available.why: Shared holiday scene reaches both.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Trading card is a compound, but star only reaches through the sports stars pictured on trading cards (or Star Wars card sets).
Ace is the top card, and ace and star are both words for a top performer, a shared-meaning route that is defensible but not a phrase.

best_available.why: Reaches card perfectly and star through the shared 'top performer' sense, which is more natural than TRADING's picture-on-the-card route.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. ACE is the closest; a second opinion could reasonably promote it.

hints.reason: Train ticket is immediate; card only follows because a ticket is a small printed card or a travel card replaces one.

best_available.why: Only hint offered; the card-as-ticket route is plausible but not a familiar phrase.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Card side is a material resemblance rather than a connection a player would name.

hints.reason: A flush is a poker hand, and to flush is to send water through.

best_available.why: Clean double meaning, both widely known.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: Tarot is a card deck, and the witch reading tarot is a familiar scene.

best_available.why: Shared fortune-telling scene.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Wild card is a compound and the wolf is the archetypal wild animal.

best_available.why: Compound plus a strong shared property.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Puss is a cat (Puss in Boots), but castle only reaches via the ogre's castle Puss wins in the tale, a detail most players do not retain.

best_available.why: Only hint offered; cat is certain and the fairy-tale setting gives castle a faint foothold.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The story route to castle is secondary to the plot rather than its centre.

hints.reason: Royal castle and royal crown share the royalty property directly.
The king lives in the castle and wears the crown.

best_available.why: A concrete figure that owns both objects.

pairs.pair_note: Both strong; the pair is nearly self-clueing.

hints.reason: A diamond is a jewel, and the crown jewels / castle treasure is a familiar fairy-tale and Tower-of-London image.

best_available.why: Diamond is immediate and jewels-in-the-castle is a recognizable scene.

pairs.pair_note: Castle side is a scene rather than a phrase, but a familiar one.

hints.reason: Castle guard and guard dog are both everyday compounds.

best_available.why: Two familiar compounds.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Humpty Dumpty is the egg; castle only arrives through the wall and the king's horses and men, which illustrations sometimes set at a castle.

best_available.why: Only hint offered; egg is certain, castle is an inference from the rhyme's royal setting.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The rhyme says wall, not castle.

hints.reason: A hearth is where the fire burns, but castle only follows from the great-hall hearth image, and hearths belong to any home.
The dragon breathes fire and besieges or guards the castle in the standard fairy-tale scene.

best_available.why: One shared story scene reaches both words at full strength.

pairs.pair_note: DRAGON carries the pair; HEARTH is a soft second.

hints.reason: A moat surrounds a castle, and fish in the moat is a recognizable image since the moat is a body of water.

best_available.why: Castle is certain and the water-to-fish step is short.

pairs.pair_note: Fish side is a one-step inference (moat is water); judged a recognizable scene rather than a stretch, but close to the line.

hints.reason: Spooky is the ghost's mood, and the spooky castle is a standard Halloween / Dracula image.
Haunted castle is a stock phrase and a haunting is done by a ghost.

best_available.why: Compound phrase on one side and the defining ghost action on the other.

pairs.pair_note: HAUNTED is clearly the better of two valid mood-based hints.

hints.reason: The glass slipper and the prince's castle (also Disney's Cinderella Castle) are both central to the story.
Glass slipper is immediate, but castle needs the extra hop through Cinderella's story.

best_available.why: Names the story so both objects fall out at once.

pairs.pair_note: CINDERELLA carries the pair; SLIPPER is a weaker variant.

hints.reason: Gold is kept in a treasury, and the castle treasury / strongroom is a recognizable medieval room.

best_available.why: Gold is immediate and the treasury-as-castle-room scene is familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Castle side depends on the medieval sense of treasury rather than the government department.

hints.reason: The Queen of Hearts (cards, Alice) reaches heart, and the queen lives in the castle.

best_available.why: Both routes are stock.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Mead is honey wine drunk in medieval castle halls, but many players will not know what mead is made from and the castle link is only a mood.

best_available.why: Only hint offered; correct on both sides but niche.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Factually sound, recognizability is the problem.

hints.reason: Horses live in stables, and the castle stables for the knights' horses are a familiar scene.
The knight rides a horse and serves in the castle.

best_available.why: A figure that belongs equally to both words.

pairs.pair_note: KNIGHT is the stronger; STABLE is fair.

hints.reason: Elsa has ice powers and builds the ice castle/palace in Frozen.
Frozen is literally ice, and the film Frozen supplies the ice castle and Arendelle castle.

best_available.why: Names the character whose signature act is the ice castle.

pairs.pair_note: Both valid; FROZEN depends on the film for the castle side.

hints.reason: Castle gate and iron gate are both stock compounds.

best_available.why: Two compounds.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: The dungeon is the castle's prison, and the dungeon key / jailer's keys is a familiar story and video-game item.

best_available.why: Castle is immediate and the key-to-the-dungeon scene is well worn.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Medieval castle and medieval knight share the period directly.
The knight is a chess piece and the rook is commonly called the castle (castling).

best_available.why: Most direct; CHESS is equally valid and more playful.

pairs.pair_note: Two good hints of different flavours.

hints.reason: A beacon is a signal light, but castle only reaches through beacon fires lit on castle towers, an image many players will not produce.

best_available.why: Only hint offered; light is certain, castle is a tower-signal inference.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Castle side is a scene without a phrase behind it.

hints.reason: Aslan the lion makes Narnia reach lion, but castle needs Cair Paravel or the White Witch's castle, details beyond the title.
The king lives in the castle and the lion is king of the jungle / The Lion King.

best_available.why: Both routes are universal.

pairs.pair_note: KING carries the pair; NARNIA is a fun but unreliable alternative.
